one_line_contribution: A regime-transplant difference-in-differences diagnostic claiming that instructions evolved by a reflective optimizer while a retrieved memory bank is injected become dependent on that specific bank (so the reported optimizer+memory gain is bank-conditional rather than owned), plus a counterfactual-replay routing rule (CCR) that sends memory-caused training failures to the write path instead of the instruction reflector.
closest_prior_work: On the mechanism, the proposal is right that CANTANTE (2605.13295) and Environment-Grounded APO (2606.17838) are the nearest threats, and it honestly concedes the counterfactual-replay signal as prior art; B9 is a fair gradient-free stand-in for UCOB/HiMPO. The larger unacknowledged threat is to the object the proposal actually claims as novel — the transplant/DiD diagnostic. 'Optimize under regime A, evaluate under regime B' is a train/test regime swap, i.e. the standard prompt-transfer ablation that MIPRO/DSPy-lineage work and 'Teach Better or Show Smarter?' already run in the instruction-vs-exemplar setting, and the RAG literature routinely reports optimized prompts degrading when the retriever or demonstration pool is swapped. Substituting 'self-editing experience bank' for 'bootstrapped demonstration set' changes the artifact but not the experimental move. Conceptually, 'co-adaptation between two jointly fitted components, removable by dropout' is the classical dropout argument, which is why B4 is the theoretically motivated fix and CCR the elaborate one. The claim 'none of them runs the transplant' is also precisely the claim the proposal admits it never searched for (the OpenReview query it could not run), so it rests on assertion.
strongest_objection: The headline quantity is not identified. DiD = [R_mem@T_mem − R_mem@T_nomem] − [R_nomem@T_mem − R_nomem@T_nomem]. The second bracket is, by this track's own prior measurement, already known to be negative: injecting the full k=7 bank into an unadapted prompt fixed zero items and broke six to seven (McNemar p=0.031/0.016). A DiD of +5 points or more can therefore be produced entirely by memory harming the memory-free instruction, with literally zero co-adaptation in the R_mem instruction — and P1's own prose gloss ('instructions optimized with memory lose more when memory is removed than memory-free instructions gain from having it') is satisfied trivially when the memory-free instruction *loses* from having memory. The proposal never states that the first bracket must be positive, never reports a precondition on it, and never separates 'k=7 injection harms any prompt' (a published result of this track) from 'this instruction has absorbed this bank' (the new claim). This compounds with a second, related problem: R_mem is deliberately trained at k=7, the exact injection volume the track already showed to be harmful and already showed to be fixable by cutting to k=3. So the co-adaptation being studied may be co-adaptation to a known pathology, and the most likely empirical outcome is that B10 (train at k=2) removes the effect — which the proposal itself concedes collapses the routing story. P2, the 'sharp, disagreeable' claim, is worse off still: a gain cannot be shown to be rented if there is no gain. P2 asserts R_mem's advantage over R_nomem at T_shift falls to ≤1 point, but nothing in the design establishes that this advantage exists at T_mem in the first place, and the track's prior data suggests it may not. As written, P2 risks being vacuously 'confirmed' by an advantage that was never there. Secondarily, the mechanism separation in P6 — the thing that distinguishes CCR from a blind regularizer, and the paper's actual method contribution — rests on B9, B10 and B5 at 3 seeds each, with no MDE stated for 3-seed conditions; with the proposal's own between-seed SD of 2.0-2.5 points, a 3-seed contrast cannot support a claim like 'B9 captures less than half of CCR's interaction reduction' or 'B4/B10 lose ≥2 points at T_mem relative to CCR'. The MDE section carefully powers the claim the authors expect to win and leaves the claims that would kill the method underpowered.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a precondition, reported before anything else, on all four Part 1 cells separately rather than only their contrast: state and test that memory injection at the chosen k actually helps (or at least does not harm) an unadapted and an R_nomem instruction, and choose k accordingly. If the second DiD bracket is negative, drop the DiD as primary and use a quantity that cannot be manufactured by injection harm — e.g. the within-R_mem T_mem→T_shift drop benchmarked against a bank-swap-matched control, with the R_mem@T_mem − R_mem@T_nomem single difference reported with its sign. (2) Report P1 at both k=7 and k=3, so the diagnostic is not confounded with the already-known volume pathology, and specify the evaluation k for B10 (as written, B10 trains at k=2 and is evaluated at T_mem k=7, which is itself a train/test regime mismatch and stacks the deck against the strongest competing intervention). (3) Add the volume-matched placebo optimization regime described in missing_baseline; without it, 'memory-referential clauses' in P3 and the DiD in P1 are both consistent with adaptation to 7 extra context items of any content. (4) Give B9 and B10 five paired seeds and publish their MDEs, or strip the numeric thresholds out of P6 and state it qualitatively; the paper's mechanism claim should not be the least-powered comparison in it. (5) The track brief says a methods contribution must overturn or qualify specific existing results. Run the transplant protocol on at least one re-implemented published memory+optimizer system (ACE-style joint loop is named as the motivating target), not only on the authors' own pipeline, or restate P2 explicitly as a claim about this pipeline rather than about 'published-style headline gains'. (6) Complete the OpenReview/transplant search and resolve 2605.28732, whose title covers Part 2 directly.
missing_baseline: Two. First, a volume-matched placebo optimization regime — R_shuf: optimize with the same k=7 injection slot filled by shuffled or task-irrelevant items of matched token volume, then transplant. The proposal lists a shuffled-bank check only as an evaluation-time sanity control, not as a training regime, so nothing in the design separates 'the instruction adapted to this bank's content' from 'the instruction adapted to having a long retrieved block in context'. Every Part 1 result and the P3 clause correlation survive equally under the null hypothesis of pure volume adaptation. Second, multi-bank / bank-resampling optimization: optimize R_mem while alternating between two or more independently written banks and evaluate on a third. This is the standard domain-randomization answer to P2's shift claim, is cheaper than CCR, and is not the same as B4 (dropout randomizes memory *presence*, not bank *identity*, so it cannot teach bank-invariance, only memory-optionality). A reviewer will ask why the obvious fix for bank-conditionality — train on more than one bank — was not the first thing tried, and if it works, CCR is unnecessary for the paper's own headline robustness claim.
preprint_collision: The best part of the submission, and unusually honest: nine items named with IDs, an explicit concession that the counterfactual-replay signal is prior art, HiMPO/CANTANTE/UCOB correctly identified as mechanism ancestors, UCOB promoted into a baseline (B9) rather than argued away, and ACE reframed as the motivating target. That is more collision work than most submissions do. But it is thorough exactly where the proposal no longer claims novelty and thin exactly where it does. The authors state plainly that both search sessions were rate-limited before any targeted query on 'transplant / difference-in-differences evaluation of optimized prompts under memory ablation' could be run — that is, the one search that bears on the claimed novel object was never executed, and the proposal itself flags this as the least-verified load-bearing item. Two further entries are unresolved: 'Tracing and Attributing Errors in LLM Memory Systems' (2605.28732), whose title covers Part 2's attribution problem and for which only a reference list was retrieved, and the ICLR 2026 counterfactual-RAG poster whose abstract was never obtained. Per the standard that an unsearched claim of novelty is a weakness rather than a neutral: the mechanism half is properly cleared and correctly de-claimed, the diagnostic half is unsearched, and the diagnostic half is the entire remaining contribution. Candor about the gap is worth credit in the clarity and integrity dimension; it does not substitute for the search.
